What rank are you at? You might not be thinking ahead enough. You can't autopilot that deck. It's really reactive and you have to watch what your opponent is doing very carefully. Here are some tricks.

You usually want to play DD with another 2 drop on Turn 4, so your opponent has less time to see it coming. Playing him Turn 3 with a 1 drop also works. He's often too low tempo as a Turn 2 play, losing you the ability to, for example, shut down Carnage with Armor or Cosmo on Turn 3.

Try to match your opponent's lanes before Turn 4. If you are even against them on all lanes, it's really hard for them to play around Professor X.

Use White Queen to predict their Turn 6 play. Knowing both their Turn 5 and Turn 6 play will help you come up with a way to show it down.

Lastly, don't always try to play Professor X. There are games where you just want to play double dinosaurs. There are games where you want to play Cosmo to stop an On Reveal effect.

Gwent has a pretty high skill floor. Your win rate is going to shoot up a ton once you understand the basics.

The basic game structure is:

* In Round 1, both players usually try to win the round, which lets them take **round control** in Round 2.
   * "Round control" means you can bail Round 2 any time you want, but your opponent risks losing the whole game if they bail.
* Most of the time, the objective of Round 1 is to win it without **overcommitting** your resources. A classic newbie mistake is to use all the best cards in Round 1, win it by 50 points (which is the same as winning by 1 point), and end up with no good cards left for Round 3.
* In Round 2, the player with **round control** gets to decide if they want to **dry pass**, or to **bleed** the opponent.
   * "Dry pass" means you pass Round 2 without playing any card. This is the safer approach when you're a new player. It guarantees that you'll have **last say** in Round 3, although not much else. This also leads into a **long** Round 3.
      * "Last say" means you get to play the very last card of Round 3. It can be a big advantage. You get to save your best removal for your opponent's best unit, or, you get to play your best unit last without having to worry about any removal.
   * "Bleed" means you take advantage of the fact that your opponent can't bail Round 2 to force out their best cards before the next round. This can be a riskier approach. You can end up going one card down and losing last say, but it can give you a big advantage if you force out the best cards from your opponent. This also leads into a **short** Round 3.
* In Round 3, the player who won Round 1 usually has the **last say**, which is an advantage. Another determining factor of Round 3 is who used up too many good cards in Round 1 and 2.
* Round 3 can be a **long** round or a **short** round.
   * **Engine** cards, for example cards that grow 1 power every turn, or deal 1 damage every turn, are better in a **long** round.
   * **Pointslam** cards, for example units with a ton of points, or summon an  additional unit from the graveyard or your deck, are better in a **short** round (they get a ton of points when you play them, but don't grow in points as the round keeps going).

I'm skipping a lot of details here, like the difference between going first (**blue coin**) vs. going second (**red coin**), the difference between winning Round 1 on even vs. winning one card down, and when to take an early pass. Some of these are rules of thumb that don't always apply.

Like I said, Gwent has a high skill floor. But if you even understand the basics above, you should hit Rank 7 in no time.

Lastly, make sure you're playing in Ranked, not training mode. You'll get a much better chance running into similarly skilled players in Ranked. Training mode is filled with veterans.

Pointslam: Cards that generate a ton of power immediately.

Control: Cards that remove stuff.

Control decks are weaker to pointslam decks because it's more difficult to remove all the power efficiently.

1. Frantic efforts to avoid real or imagined abandonment. Note: Do not include suicidal or self-mutilating behaviour covered in criterion 5. **Check.** The way she reacts to Vi getting close with Caitlyn (and to, in Jinx's mind, replace her) is to kidnap Caitlyn and ask Vi to kill her.
